def-regular-generalized-eigenvalue-penci.empty: Definition explicitly assumes n>=1, so a zero-order pencil is outside the domain; projective coordinates must not both vanish.
def-regular-generalized-eigenvalue-penci.one: Definition allows n=1, where det(beta*A-alpha*B) is the scalar linear expression; beta=0 is retained as an infinite pair and only(0,0) is excluded.
def-regular-generalized-eigenvalue-penci.nonempty-choice: The pencil is specified by the two given matrices; its projective root set is defined as a quotient, without choosing one representative in each class.
def-regular-generalized-eigenvalue-penci.logic: The item defines regularity by a nonzero determinant polynomial and finite/infinite homogeneous coordinates; it asserts no additional algorithm-success or convergence equivalence.

lem-block-upper-triangular-pencil-determ.zero: Proof step1.1 uses zero lower-left entries to eliminate permutation terms, and step2.1 sums the remaining terms; no matrix or scalar parameter is divided by, so alpha=0 or beta=0 causes no singular-denominator issue.
lem-block-upper-triangular-pencil-determ.degenerate: Statement requires positive two-block sizes but no invertibility of either diagonal block; proof step2.1 permits either determinant factor to vanish and then the product identity is zero on both sides.
lem-block-upper-triangular-pencil-determ.endpoints: The block-determinant identity is algebraic for every complex alpha,beta, with no real interval, tolerance or limiting endpoint parameter.
lem-block-upper-triangular-pencil-determ.nonempty-choice: The finite Leibniz permutation sum is prescribed by the block partition, and factoring it chooses no eigenvalue, eigenvector or basis family.
lem-block-upper-triangular-pencil-determ.logic: The claim is a determinant product identity for a given two-block triangular pair, not an equivalence between regularity and any spectral or algorithmic condition.

lem-zero-determinant-matrix-has-nonzero-.empty: Statement n>=1 excludes the empty determinant convention; the conclusion concerns a genuine nonzero vector in an actual positive-dimensional kernel.
lem-zero-determinant-matrix-has-nonzero-.one: For n=1 a zero determinant is a zero scalar, and the rank/invertibility contradiction in proof steps1.1–2.1 yields a nonzero scalar kernel vector, as required.
lem-zero-determinant-matrix-has-nonzero-.degenerate: Proof step1.1 supposes the kernel were zero, derives injectivity and surjectivity in equal finite dimensions, and step2.1 contradicts det(M)=0; arbitrary rank deficiency is admitted.
lem-zero-determinant-matrix-has-nonzero-.endpoints: No continuous parameter or interval appears in the zero-determinant implication; its excluded boundary is matrix order0, already ruled out by n>=1.
lem-zero-determinant-matrix-has-nonzero-.nonempty-choice: The conclusion is existential for one finite-dimensional kernel, obtained by contradiction from rank/invertibility; it does not select vectors simultaneously for a family of singular matrices.
lem-zero-determinant-matrix-has-nonzero-.logic: This lemma proves det(M)=0 implies one nonzero kernel vector. The opposite determinant implication is not stated as a second direction here.

def-b-inner-product-and-dual-norm-for-de.empty: Definition assumes a Hermitian positive-definite B with its Cholesky factor. It defines products and norms, not a minimum over an independently supplied possibly empty eigenset.
def-b-inner-product-and-dual-norm-for-de.one: Definition for a positive scalar B=b uses L=sqrt(b)>0, giving sqrt(b)|x| and |r|/sqrt(b); neither inverse is taken at zero b.
def-b-inner-product-and-dual-norm-for-de.degenerate: The Cholesky factor has positive diagonal, so B and L are invertible. The norm definitions permit x=0 and r=0, but exclude a singular or merely semidefinite B from their hypotheses.
def-b-inner-product-and-dual-norm-for-de.endpoints: The metric definition has no time or tolerance interval; positivity of B, rather than a limiting semidefinite endpoint, supplies its inverse and Cholesky factors.
def-b-inner-product-and-dual-norm-for-de.nonempty-choice: The Cholesky factor named in the Definition is unique with positive diagonal; the B metric and dual norm are then fixed, with no arbitrary factor or eigenbasis selection.
def-b-inner-product-and-dual-norm-for-de.logic: Definition explicitly says x*By=0 is equivalent to <x,y>_B=0. Since <x,y>_B=y*Bx=conjugate(x*By) for Hermitian B, conjugation sends zero to zero in both directions; the quoted Cholesky theorem's iff in its ID is not a separate new obligation.

alg-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-re.empty: Definition n>=1 permits n=1, when both rotation index lists are empty and Q=Z=I already give the scalar Hessenberg-triangular pair.
alg-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-re.one: Definition with n=1 runs no two-row/column target actions and returns its scalar arrays and identity factor records.
alg-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-re.zero: Definition first chooses I2 at a=b=0; otherwise r>0, and its complex a=0 branch divides by |b| only when b!=0. Thus all normalization divisors are guarded.
alg-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-re.degenerate: Definition admits singular A or B and zero target pairs: identity branches preserve them. Exact transformations are recorded products, without asserting rounded dense unitarity.
alg-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-re.endpoints: The reduction has only finite integer loop boundaries. Its last Givens target and n=1 empty schedules are explicit, rather than a real parameter endpoint claim.
alg-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-re.logic: The algorithm specifies deterministic left/right transformations and their returned arrays; no converse asserts that any equivalent Hessenberg pair must come from this execution.

def-generalized-schur-form.empty: Definition is for a regular finite pencil; the in-page regular-pencil convention has positive order, so diagonal block roots are not assigned to an empty input pair.
def-generalized-schur-form.one: Definition allows a one-by-one nonzero homogeneous diagonal pair, including second coordinate0 for an infinite generalized eigenvalue.
def-generalized-schur-form.zero: Definition excludes a singular pencil and requires each real one-by-one diagonal pair nonzero, while permitting T_ii=0 and hence an infinite pair; it never divides by that zero coordinate.
def-generalized-schur-form.nonempty-choice: This item defines what given Q,Z,S,T constitute a generalized Schur form; existence of such factors is a separate theorem rather than an unspecified selection in this definition.
def-generalized-schur-form.logic: Complex and real generalized Schur forms are factorization predicates with stated block conventions, not an iff between a rounded diagnostic and an exact original-input decomposition.

lem-projective-determinant-is-homogeneou.empty: Statement assumes n>=1, fixing a positive number of determinant columns; its homogeneous scaling identity itself still includes c=0.
lem-projective-determinant-is-homogeneou.one: Proof step1.1 scales each of n columns, and for n=1 this is the single scalar factor c; no higher-order block induction is needed.
lem-projective-determinant-is-homogeneou.zero: Proof step1.1 includes c=0 in the homogeneous polynomial identity. Step2.1 invokes c!=0 only for equivalence of zero conditions and beta!=0 before the finite ratio alpha/beta.
lem-projective-determinant-is-homogeneou.degenerate: The determinant identity needs no regularity or invertibility of A or B; an identically zero pencil polynomial also satisfies it. Only representative rescaling and finite-ratio divisions require their stated nonzero scalars.
lem-projective-determinant-is-homogeneou.nonempty-choice: Projective invariance is proved for any supplied nonzero rescaling, not by choosing canonical representatives for an entire quotient set.
lem-projective-determinant-is-homogeneou.logic: Proof step2.1 uses p(c*alpha,c*beta)=c^n p(alpha,beta) and c^n!=0, proving both directions of vanishing equivalence for nonzero representative changes.

lem-regular-pencil-has-no-common-kernel-.empty: The regular-pencil convention has positive order; proof step2.1 compares the determinant polynomial's at-most-n roots with more than n explicit complex numbers, not an empty spectral list.
lem-regular-pencil-has-no-common-kernel-.one: For order1, a shared nonzero scalar kernel vector would force both scalar matrices zero, and proof steps1.1–2.1 give the same contradiction to regularity.
lem-regular-pencil-has-no-common-kernel-.zero: Proof step1.1 intentionally starts with Ax=Bx=0 and supposes x!=0; it never divides by either matrix or the vector, so singular B is not excluded.
lem-regular-pencil-has-no-common-kernel-.degenerate: Regularity excludes the common nonzero kernel even if one of A or B is singular; the determinant-root-count contradiction in step2.1 requires no definite or invertible B.
lem-regular-pencil-has-no-common-kernel-.endpoints: The common-kernel argument is an exact finite algebraic implication, with no time, sweep or tolerance endpoint parameter.
lem-regular-pencil-has-no-common-kernel-.nonempty-choice: Assuming one particular nonzero common kernel vector for contradiction is not choosing a vector for every matrix pencil; finite polynomial root counting supplies the contradiction.
lem-regular-pencil-has-no-common-kernel-.logic: The lemma proves that regularity rules out a nonzero common kernel; it does not assert that absence of a common kernel is sufficient for pencil regularity.

lem-two-sided-unitary-equivalence-errors.empty: Proof step1.1 explicitly handles m=0 by Q=Z=I and Delta_A=Delta_B=0, so empty products and the empty error sum have their actual base values.
lem-two-sided-unitary-equivalence-errors.one: For m=1 the supplied local update is already the global update; proof step2.1's augmented block-matrix norm is exactly the one pair error norm.
lem-two-sided-unitary-equivalence-errors.zero: Proof step1.1 permits zero local arithmetic/deflation arrays and zero accumulated perturbation; its transport uses unitary factors, not division by an error norm.
lem-two-sided-unitary-equivalence-errors.degenerate: Proof step2.1 depends on norm preservation of the supplied unitary products, with no invertibility of A or B. Exact zero perturbations remain zero and tolerance errors are counted additively.
lem-two-sided-unitary-equivalence-errors.endpoints: The accumulation lemma ends after a supplied nonnegative integer m of local updates; its m=0 endpoint is explicitly proved, not an omitted limiting real endpoint.
lem-two-sided-unitary-equivalence-errors.nonempty-choice: Proof step1.1 constructs the augmented arrays directly and step2.1 reads off their accumulated blocks; no arbitrary perturbation selector is needed.
lem-two-sided-unitary-equivalence-errors.logic: The result composes given local two-sided update identities into one global perturbed identity; matrix equivalence names the relation, not a logical biconditional to direction-check.

thm-hermitian-definite-pencil-has-real-s.empty: The definite-pencil result uses the positive-order in-page matrix convention and a positive-definite B, so it supplies a genuine eigenbasis; no minimum over an empty spectrum appears here.
thm-hermitian-definite-pencil-has-real-s.one: For order1 the Cholesky transform in proof step1.1 yields a single real self-adjoint scalar; step3.1 transports its unit vector to one B-normalized generalized mode.
thm-hermitian-definite-pencil-has-real-s.degenerate: Proof step1.1 proves L invertible from its positive diagonal; step4.1 uses det(B)!=0 to exclude an infinite pair. Repeated real eigenvalues remain allowed by the self-adjoint eigenbasis supplier.
thm-hermitian-definite-pencil-has-real-s.endpoints: This exact definite-pencil theorem has no iteration or tolerance endpoint; a merely semidefinite B is outside the positive-definite hypothesis needed before the inverse.
thm-hermitian-definite-pencil-has-real-s.nonempty-choice: The proof invokes the finite-dimensional real/complex spectral theorem for one self-adjoint Cholesky transform and transports that one basis; no choice of eigenbases for an infinite pencil family is asserted.
thm-hermitian-definite-pencil-has-real-s.logic: The theorem provides real generalized eigenvalues and a B-orthogonal basis under Hermitian-definite assumptions, not an iff characterization of every pencil possessing a real spectrum.

prop-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-r.empty: Proof step2.1 treats the first Hessenberg column's absence of earlier columns as vacuous; for n=1 the Definition's loops are empty and identity factors give the required form.
prop-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-r.one: At n=1 there is only a scalar array and no annihilation target; the invariant A_current=Q* A_input Z in proof step3.1 holds with Q=Z=I.
prop-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-r.zero: The invoked exact Givens Definition uses identity at a zero target pair. Proof steps1.1–2.1 preserve already-zero entries and do not normalize them again without the guard.
prop-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-r.degenerate: Proof step2.1 allows newly created bulges but shows the paired right rotation removes the one B fill; singular or zero arrays do not invalidate this support induction.
prop-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-r.endpoints: The descending rotation schedules stop at their stated boundary rows; proof step3.1 ranges only over j=1,...,n-2, including the empty schedule for small order.
prop-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-r.nonempty-choice: The source algorithm defines each Givens factor deterministically, including its zero branch, so the proof's finite support induction introduces no set-theoretic selection.
prop-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-r.logic: The proposition establishes termination, target matrix form and two-sided transformation identities; it does not assert that every equivalent pair is generated by the given schedule.

lem-regular-pencil-has-projective-eigenv.empty: Regularity makes the determinant polynomial nonzero, while positive order ensures either its full positive degree has a complex root or its missing leading coefficient yields the explicit infinite pair[1:0].
lem-regular-pencil-has-projective-eigenv.one: For a scalar regular pencil, proof step2.1 gives the ordinary finite root when degree1, and step2.2 gives[1:0] when the scalar B is zero.
lem-regular-pencil-has-projective-eigenv.zero: Proof step2.2 permits det(B)=0 and constructs an infinite pair instead of dividing by a zero beta; neither constructed homogeneous pair is(0,0).
lem-regular-pencil-has-projective-eigenv.degenerate: The degree-drop case in proof step2.2 includes a constant nonzero determinant polynomial, such as a regular pencil with B=0; it still supplies the infinite homogeneous root.
lem-regular-pencil-has-projective-eigenv.nonempty-choice: Proof step2.1 uses existence of one root of one complex polynomial, and step2.2 constructs[1:0] explicitly. No simultaneous selection across a family of pencils is needed.
lem-regular-pencil-has-projective-eigenv.logic: The projective-root lemma gives existence for regular pencils; it does not claim that having a homogeneous root characterizes regularity, since singular pencils are excluded by hypothesis.

thm-b-metric-residual-encloses-definite-.empty: Statement n>=1 and positive-definite B give at least one real generalized eigenvalue from the finite eigenbasis; the distance minimum is over a nonempty finite spectrum.
thm-b-metric-residual-encloses-definite-.one: Proof step2.1's orthonormal expansion includes n=1 and then consists of the single scalar residual coefficient, so its distance bound becomes the scalar absolute error estimate.
thm-b-metric-residual-encloses-definite-.degenerate: Statement requires x!=0. Proof step1.1 sends x to y=L*x, which is nonzero because L is invertible; the final division is by its positive B norm. Zero residual is allowed and gives an exact spectral point.
thm-b-metric-residual-encloses-definite-.nonempty-choice: The distance is the minimum over the finite supplied generalized eigenbasis spectrum, so an attaining eigenvalue exists without a selector for an infinite family.
thm-b-metric-residual-encloses-definite-.logic: The last sentence restates distance<=radius as containment in a centered real interval; proof step2.1 supplies the distance estimate, and the finite real spectrum makes the containment restatement valid in both directions.

alg-finite-budget-qz-iteration-with-defl.empty: Definition n>=1 keeps an actual input pencil; it explicitly allows N=0, which executes initialization/deflation but performs no step4 sweep before its budget status.
alg-finite-budget-qz-iteration-with-defl.one: Definition scans isolated one-by-one diagonal pairs: a nonzero first coordinate with second0 is an infinite candidate, while(0,0) returns singular-pencil-suspected without an eigenvalue.
alg-finite-budget-qz-iteration-with-defl.logic: The computed QZ algorithm reports finite statuses and conditional residual certificates; no logical iff identifies a tolerance-induced candidate with an exact original-input generalized eigenvalue.

thm-generalized-schur-form-exists-for-re.empty: Proof step1.1 permits an empty trailing pencil after removing the final block; steps4.1–5.1 explicitly avoid applying a positive-size block factorization or another induction step to that empty remainder.
thm-generalized-schur-form-exists-for-re.nonempty-choice: The proof makes finitely many eigenvector and orthonormal-completion choices while the pencil order decreases by one or two; these are finite-dimensional existence steps, not an asserted choice of forms for an infinite family.
thm-generalized-schur-form-exists-for-re.logic: Proof step6.1 factors the homogeneous determinant into nonzero block determinants. A full determinant vanishes exactly when at least one diagonal factor vanishes, proving both inclusions of the claimed generalized-root set equality.

prop-finite-budget-qz-iteration-terminat.empty: Proof step1.3 counts finite initialization, at most n infinite removals and at most N sweeps; the source N=0 branch omits sweeps without requiring an empty input matrix.
prop-finite-budget-qz-iteration-terminat.one: Proof step3.1 requires each returned diagonal pair nonzero; in order1 this is the single linear homogeneous factor and(0,0) has already exited by the mandatory scan.
prop-finite-budget-qz-iteration-terminat.zero: Proof step1.2 checks an isolated(0,0) pair and returns singular-pencil-suspected without assigning an eigenvalue; zero T diagonals with a nonzero H entry instead use the infinite-isolation branch.
prop-finite-budget-qz-iteration-terminat.degenerate: Proof step2.2 asserts a perturbed equivalence only for certified exact-unitary factor records; missing range or factor certificates terminate with a declared failure rather than becoming an unqualified accuracy theorem.
prop-finite-budget-qz-iteration-terminat.nonempty-choice: Active blocks are processed in the source's fixed order and a finite supplied shift branch; the proof counts these explicit actions and selects no global Schur form from an infinite family.
prop-finite-budget-qz-iteration-terminat.logic: Pencil equivalence in this proposition denotes its two-sided matrix relation, not a biconditional between execution status and spectral accuracy; the last clause expressly withholds an error-size bound.

thm-computed-qz-pair-has-certified-backw.empty: The supplied finite local update list may have no stages; the accumulated lemma's empty-product base gives identity factors and zero local error, while the independent raw residual formula still has its stated meaning.
thm-computed-qz-pair-has-certified-backw.one: Proof step1.2 works for one scalar matrix pair or one local factor, using the same exact unitary norm preservation as in larger dimensions.
thm-computed-qz-pair-has-certified-backw.zero: Proof step1.2 constructs Delta_A=-Q R_A Z* and Delta_B=-Q R_B Z* directly; zero residuals give zero backward perturbations without dividing by their norms.
thm-computed-qz-pair-has-certified-backw.degenerate: Proof step2.1 counts structural writes inside local arithmetic error and separate tolerance writes only once; step3.1 permits the residual route to fail without invalidating another independently certified local route.
thm-computed-qz-pair-has-certified-backw.endpoints: The backward-error theorem has no time horizon; it retains exact finite deflation entries even at a tolerance threshold and makes no O(u) assertion for those writes.
thm-computed-qz-pair-has-certified-backw.nonempty-choice: The independent perturbations in proof step1.2 are explicit products of the returned exact factor records and raw residuals, not an arbitrary existence selection.
thm-computed-qz-pair-has-certified-backw.logic: This theorem supplies two sufficient backward-certificate routes under their own hypotheses; it does not characterize every implementation or claim that an unavailable certificate disproves a small error.

ex-singular-b-yields-an-infinite-general.empty: Example fixes a two-by-two pair A=I,B=diag(1,0), so its homogeneous determinant beta*(beta-alpha) is not an empty product.
ex-singular-b-yields-an-infinite-general.one: Verification step2.1 explicitly yields one finite projective root[1:1] and one infinite root[1:0]; beta0 is not removed by a finite-ratio division.
ex-singular-b-yields-an-infinite-general.nonempty-choice: Both generalized root classes are written explicitly from the two scalar determinant factors; no abstract root or basis selection is used.
ex-singular-b-yields-an-infinite-general.logic: The witness shows singular B is compatible with a regular pencil, not an iff characterization of pencil regularity by singularity of B.

ex-regular-and-singular-pencil-determina.empty: Both examples are fixed two-by-two pairs; verification step1.1 has determinant1 and step2.1 has the identically zero determinant, so an empty matrix convention is irrelevant.
ex-regular-and-singular-pencil-determina.one: Verification step1.1 produces the single projective root class[1:0] with multiplicity two for beta^2; it does not misidentify a second distinct finite root.
ex-regular-and-singular-pencil-determina.nonempty-choice: The determinant witnesses use A=I2 or diag(1,0) and B=0 explicitly, with direct scalar determinant evaluations and no eigenvector selection.
ex-regular-and-singular-pencil-determina.logic: The example contrasts two pencils sharing singular B but different determinant polynomials; it does not claim a necessary-and-sufficient rule based on B alone.

ex-mass-stiffness-pencil-has-two-b-ortho.empty: Example fixes two-by-two positive mass/stiffness matrices; verification step1.1 factors the nonzero determinant into two actual finite roots1 and4.
ex-mass-stiffness-pencil-has-two-b-ortho.one: Verification step3.1 uses the single trial vector e1 and trial value2, with residual(0,-2); the distance to the two-root spectrum is1 and the proved bound is sqrt2.
ex-mass-stiffness-pencil-has-two-b-ortho.endpoints: The mass-stiffness witness has no time interval or tolerance cap; its trial spectral center2 and norm ratio are explicit finite quantities.
ex-mass-stiffness-pencil-has-two-b-ortho.nonempty-choice: The two modes(1,1),(1,-2), the trial vector and residual are all displayed, so neither an orthogonal-basis selector nor a minimizing-eigenvalue choice is left implicit.
ex-mass-stiffness-pencil-has-two-b-ortho.logic: This concrete definite-pencil calculation verifies two modes and one residual enclosure; it does not state a biconditional characterization of all mass-stiffness discretizations.
